links.comparator_used: Original GPT-3.5 scoring prompts and interaction protocol before refinement, compared against physician scoring
links.outcome: Agreement of GPT-3.5 scores with physician scores on memory and language assessments
links.effect: Before refinement, GPT-3.5 differed from physicians in memory (8 of 21 sections, P<0.05) and language in healthy subjects (P=0.009), and in language in stroke subjects (P=0.002). After refinement, differences remained only in memory sections 8 and 14 (P<0.05), with no significant differences in the rest (P>0.05).
links.tradeoff: Refinement needed extra conversations (two for healthy subjects, one for stroke subjects). Memory differences in sections 8 and 14 remained. Refinement was tuned on the same discrepancies it was then tested on, and no cost or latency was reported.
links.quote: After testing, optimizing the interaction process and scoring rules can reduce most of the differences, with only differences observed in 8th and 14th sections of memory ( P < 0.05), and no significant differences observed in the rest ( P > 0.05) ( Figure 6 ).

design_hint: refined scoring protocols and interaction prompts
